```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 4,
  fig.align = "center",
  fig.retina = 2,
  out.width = "100%",
  cache.extra = packageVersion("interactmeta")
)

# Set fig.width / fig.height on the *next* chunk from [forestplot_height()].
.vig_forest_chunk <- function(fp, width = 7) {
  d <- forestplot_height(fp, width = width)
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = d$width, fig.height = d$height)
  invisible(fp)
}
```

This vignette follows the software-paper illustrations [@panaro2025cams]:
immunotherapy-by-age on `age`, then REACT corticosteroids on `steroids`,
including trial-level shrinkage and incomplete subgroup designs.

## Immunotherapy by age (`age`)

The `age` table is from a review of disease-modifying immunotherapies in
relapsing–remitting multiple sclerosis [@heesen2024]: do treatments reduce
relapses equally in Younger and Older patients when only aggregate subgroup
summaries are available? Published tables quote incidence rate ratios; values
below one favour immunotherapy. Trial ADVANCE anchors the shrinkage figures in
the paper (`?shrinkage`).

```{r age-advance, warning=FALSE}
library(interactmeta)

age[age$study == "ADVANCE", c("study", "subgroup", "yi", "vi")]
```

`age` uses `study` and `subgroup` for trial and level names. In [cams()] and
[ifrac()] you can remap columns with `trial` / `subgroup` or pass a single
`modifier` column instead of `subgroup`.

With reference Younger, `ifrac()` adds `IF_Older` $=\pi_j$ on each row
[@panaro2025cams].

```{r age-ifrac}
des_age <- ifrac(age, reference = "Younger")

des_age[des_age$study == "ADVANCE",
        c("study", "level", "yi", "vi", "IF_Older")]
```

`contrast = NULL` keeps subgroup rows only (wide `IF_*` columns).
`include_interaction = TRUE` appends within-trial contrast rows; `contrast =
c("Older", "Younger")` targets one contrast. [`?ifrac`] documents `big_var`,
`contrast_sep`, and `include_combined`.

For ADVANCE, `IF_Older` is approximately $0.268$. The Bayesian CAMS fit below
uses half-normal priors on $\tau$ and $\tau_\gamma$ as in the paper
[@panaro2026priors] (not the package's improper defaults).

```{r fit-age, cache = TRUE}
fit_age <- cams(
  des_age,
  reference = "Younger",
  tau.prior = function(tau) bayesmeta::dhalfnormal(tau, scale = 0.5),
  tau.interaction.prior = function(tau_gamma)
    bayesmeta::dhalfnormal(tau_gamma, scale = 0.1)
)

print(fit_age)
```

Without custom priors, Bayesian [cams()] uses improper uniform $\tau$ priors
(matching **bayesmeta** defaults). Set `method = "REML"` or `"ML"` for a
**metafor** fit, or `fixed.prior` for normal priors on block
means. `precompute = TRUE` warms caches eagerly; `lazy_latent =
TRUE` (default) defers latent convolves until [summary()], [tidy()], or plotting.
Pass `fit_args = list(n_support = …)` to control quadrature resolution.

```{r age-contribution, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, cache = TRUE}
plot(fit_age, type = "contribution", exponentiate = TRUE)
```

The horizontal axis is the IF assigned to Older patients (precision-based, not
enrolment share). The same [plot()] method offers `type = "heterogeneity"` ($\tau$
components) and `type = "forest"` (modifier panels). Use `exponentiate = TRUE` on
log-scale outcomes (IRR / OR); `at` or `ifrac` on the plot match [modifiers()]
and [combined()].

```{r age-forest-mod-prep, include = FALSE, cache = TRUE}
.vig_fp_age_mod <- forestplot(fit_age, type = "modifiers", exponentiate = TRUE)
.vig_forest_chunk(.vig_fp_age_mod, width = 7)
```

```{r age-forest-mod, echo = FALSE, cache = FALSE}
.vig_fp_age_mod
```

```{r age-forest-int-prep, include = FALSE, cache = TRUE}
.vig_fp_age_int <- forestplot(fit_age, type = "interaction", exponentiate = TRUE)
.vig_forest_chunk(.vig_fp_age_int, width = 7)
```

```{r age-forest-int, echo = FALSE, cache = FALSE}
.vig_fp_age_int
```

The modifier forest defaults to `type = "modifiers"` (reference and
non-reference panels, optional **Combined** via `include_combined`). The
interaction forest uses `type = "interaction"`. Toggle layers with
`include_shrinkage`, `include_overall`, and `include_prediction`; pass
`include_shrinkage = FALSE` to drop grey CAMS shrinkage rows. Set `n_var = "n"`
for a patient-count column, `group = "trial"` to nest by study, or `favours =
FALSE` to omit directional labels. Pooled summary diamonds follow `ifrac =
"interaction"` by default; see the steroids section for `ifrac = "overall"`.

Grey diamonds on the modifier forest are trial-level CAMS shrinkage at each
$\pi_j$ ([shrinkage()] with `type = "modifiers"` or `"interaction"`; same labels
as [forestplot()]).

## REACT corticosteroids (`steroids`)

The `steroids` table is from the WHO REACT meta-analysis of systemic
corticosteroids for COVID-19 mortality [@stern2020react]. Subgroups are IMV and
Non-IMV; some trials report only one ventilation stratum (not missing data).
Values below one on the exponentiated scale favour corticosteroids.

```{r steroids-escalc, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(metafor)

steroids_es <- escalc(
  measure = "OR",
  ai = treat.events, bi = treat.total - treat.events,
  ci = cont.events, di = cont.total - cont.events,
  data = steroids
)
des <- ifrac(steroids_es, reference = "Non-IMV")
```

Any [`metafor::escalc`] layout works if `yi` and `vi` are on the long table.
`ifrac()` accepts [`escalc`] output or a data frame; override `trial` /
`modifier` when column names differ from `study` / `level`. The design step is
the same as for `age`: choose `reference`, then optional `contrast` and
`include_interaction` before [cams()].

For IMV-only trials, `ifrac()` adds a high-variance placeholder (`big_var`,
default $10^4$ on the log scale). For RECOVERY, the reported IMV row is retained
and Non-IMV is filled with `yi = 0`, `vi = 10000`.

```{r recovery-placeholder}
des[des$study == "RECOVERY", c("study", "level", "yi", "vi")]
```

Tune `big_var` when single-arm imputations are too influential or too diffuse.
[cams()] also accepts `contrast_sep` and `big_var` so the fit stage matches the
design object.

CAMS separates within-trial interactions $g_j$ and combined coordinates $m_j$
[@panaro2025cams]. Heterogeneity $\tau$ and $\tau_\gamma$ are separate blocks;
see [`vignette("heterogeneity-after-cams")`](heterogeneity-after-cams.html).

```{r fit-reml, cache = TRUE}
fit_reml <- cams(des, reference = "Non-IMV", method = "REML")
```

This line uses frequentist REML; `method = "ML"` is also supported. The default
`method = "Bayesian"` path matches the `age` section ([cams()] picks **bayesmeta**
or **metafor** from `method`).

```{r summary}
print(fit_reml)
```

[summary()] and [print()] honour `digits` and `prob`. [summary()] can
`exponentiate = TRUE` for ratio-scale reporting. For one long export table,
[tidy()] collects interaction, modifier, combined, and heterogeneity rows.

At the default interaction-weighted reporting IF:

```{r estimands-reml-1}
interactions(fit_reml, type = "Overall", exponentiate = TRUE)
```

```{r estimands-reml-2}
modifiers(fit_reml, type = "Overall", exponentiate = TRUE)
```

```{r estimands-reml-3}
combined(fit_reml, type = "Overall", exponentiate = TRUE)
```

```{r estimands-reml-4}
ifrac(fit_reml, ifrac = "interaction")
```

[interactions()] is free of the reporting IF; [modifiers()] and [combined()]
pool at `ifrac = "interaction"` (default) or `ifrac = "overall"`. Instead of
pooling, pass an explicit combined IF with `at = …`. Request `type =
c("Overall", "Prediction")` for new-trial prediction intervals. Change `prob` for
other coverage levels; set `shrinkage = TRUE` to return trial-level CAMS
shrinkage tables from the same calls.

REML estimates of $\tau$ and $\tau_\gamma$ can be zero on this example, so
prediction intervals may coincide with pooled confidence intervals; that does
not establish absence of heterogeneity in general.

```{r forest-prep, include = FALSE, cache = TRUE}
.vig_fp_steroids <- forestplot(
  fit_reml,
  type = "modifiers",
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  favours = c("Lower mortality", "Higher mortality")
)
.vig_forest_chunk(.vig_fp_steroids, width = 7)
```

```{r forest, echo = FALSE, cache = FALSE}
.vig_fp_steroids
```

`favours` sets left/right benefit labels under the axis; with `favours = NULL`,
defaults follow `outcome = "unfavorable"` or `"favorable"`. Frequentist forests
omit shrinkage rows unless you refit with a Bayesian `method`. Pre-build with
[forestplot()] and size the device with [forestplot_height()] before saving or
knitting figures.

Trial-level $\pi_j$ and the pooled interaction are unchanged when the reporting
IF changes. Evaluating modifiers and forests at the overall-effect-weighted
fraction moves pooled summaries along the same fitted curves:

```{r ifrac-overall}
ifrac(fit_reml, ifrac = "overall")
modifiers(fit_reml, ifrac = "overall", exponentiate = TRUE, type = "Overall")
combined(fit_reml, ifrac = "overall", exponentiate = TRUE, type = "Overall")
```

```{r forest-overall-prep, include = FALSE, cache = TRUE}
.vig_fp_steroids_overall <- forestplot(
  fit_reml,
  type = "modifiers",
  ifrac = "overall",
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  favours = c("Lower mortality", "Higher mortality")
)
.vig_forest_chunk(.vig_fp_steroids_overall, width = 7)
```

```{r forest-overall, echo = FALSE, cache = FALSE}
.vig_fp_steroids_overall
```

Here [forestplot()] passes `ifrac = "overall"` so pooled **Overall** /
**Prediction** diamonds and x-axis annotations use overall-effect weights, while
observed study rows stay at each trial’s $\pi_j$. The same `ifrac` switch applies
in [modifiers()], [combined()], and [plot()].
